title: Raw Feeding Calculator: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Raw Feeding Calculator](/raw-feeding-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. How much raw food per day? Daily raw feeding amount for your dog. Enter your dog's weight (kg), life stage and activity level and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

How much raw food should a dog eat per day? The standard raw-feeding rule is 2–3% of body weight per day for an adult dog — 2% for low activity, 2.5% for moderate, 3% for a very active or working dog — and about 6% for a puppy. Enter your dog's weight, life stage and activity level for the daily amount in grams, split across meals, and the weekly total. The result is an estimate: adjust it if your dog gains or loses weight, and ask your vet before changing diets.

## How to use the Raw Feeding Calculator

Start by entering your dog's weight (kg), then choosing your life stage from the list and finally choosing your activity level from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter your dog's weight in kilograms.
2. Pick adult or puppy, and the activity level.
3. Read the daily amount, the per-meal amount and the weekly total.

## Formula

Daily raw food = body weight × feeding rate (2% low, 2.5% moderate, 3% high activity; about 6% for puppies).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Raw Feeding Calculator](/raw-feeding-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 20 kg moderately active adult dog needs 2.5% of its weight — 500 g of raw food per day, or 250 g per meal over two meals. Try the same figures in the [Raw Feeding Calculator](/raw-feeding-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Dog's weight (kg): 20, Life stage: Adult, Activity level: Moderate — daily walks and play), the [Raw Feeding Calculator](/raw-feeding-calculator) returns Daily raw food: 500 g per day, Feeding rate: 2.5% of body weight, Per meal: 250 g × 2 meals, Weekly amount: 3.5 kg per week. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Random Picker](/random-picker) is worth a look before you finish.

## The 2–3% rule

Raw feeding (BARF) is usually measured as a percentage of body weight because a dog's energy needs scale with size. The 2–3% range covers most adults; puppies need much more relative to their weight because they are growing. The percentages are a starting point — a dog that gains weight on 2.5% should drop to 2%, and one that loses weight should go up.

## What counts as raw food

A balanced raw diet is not just muscle meat: it includes raw meaty bones, organs (about 10% of the diet, half of it liver) and a small amount of vegetables. An all-meat diet without bones or organs is unbalanced and can cause deficiencies. If you are new to raw feeding, ask your vet or a canine nutritionist to check the diet.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Weigh your dog monthly and adjust the percentage if its weight drifts.
- Split the daily amount into two meals for adults, three for puppies.
- Raw diets need bones and organs too — meat alone is not balanced.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much raw food should I feed my dog?

About 2–3% of body weight per day for an adult dog (2% low activity, 2.5% moderate, 3% high), and about 6% for a puppy. A 20 kg moderately active dog needs about 500 g per day. Try it with your own numbers in the [Raw Feeding Calculator](/raw-feeding-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How many meals a day for a raw-fed dog?

Two meals for adults, three for puppies. Split the daily amount evenly between meals. Try it with your own numbers in the [Raw Feeding Calculator](/raw-feeding-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is raw food better than kibble?

There is no strong evidence either way. What matters is that the diet is complete and balanced — raw diets need bones and organs, not just meat. Ask your vet before switching. Try it with your own numbers in the [Raw Feeding Calculator](/raw-feeding-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Raw Feeding Calculator use?

Daily raw food = body weight × feeding rate (2% low, 2.5% moderate, 3% high activity; about 6% for puppies). You can see it in action in the [Raw Feeding Calculator](/raw-feeding-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
